questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that is blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, your car will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 or older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes. You can do this only if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars are passing you on both sides. What should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On a road with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic around you, use the right lane.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually what color?
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic. They are usually white with black markings. You must always obey these signs.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly, as this could cause a collision.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar place, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Know only the general direction of your destination.
Always choose the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip before you leave. Do not start driving with only a vague idea of where you are going. Check a map to find your destination before you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn left. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow on a traffic light?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow tells you that you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with no traffic signals at the same time as vehicles to your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic signals or signs, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Other drivers go in the order they arrived.

questions.question: If a traffic light shows a red light and a green arrow at the same time, you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow until the red light changes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: After you yield to other traffic in the intersection or crosswalk, you can turn in the direction the green arrow points. You can do this even if other lights are showing red.

questions.question: You must pull over to the edge of the road and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter what direction you are traveling.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you from the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Do this whether the vehicle is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, do not slam on the brakes or make sharp, quick turns. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Scan ahead and around to spot possible dangers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan ahead and around to spot possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead down the road for possible hazards. Staring only at the road in front of your car is dangerous. Scan ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: If you see heavy smoke covering the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beam headlights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Drive as far to the right as you can and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be deadly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, pay attention, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When passing, you should move back into the right lane when:

options.text: You are one car length ahead of the passed vehicle.
You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only pass if you have enough space to return safely to the right lane. Make sure you have enough room between you and the vehicle you passed. When you see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the right lane.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: More distance between your vehicle and others gives you more time to react. Keep a three-second following distance in normal conditions. Increase this distance if weather or traffic is bad.

questions.question: Pentagonal signs show:
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn that you are in a school zone. Watch carefully for children and pedestrians.

questions.question: When you cannot see clearly, your first action should be:

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly, slow down first. This is your most important response to poor visibility and dangerous road conditions.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: In the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle. This keeps you away from both hazards.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes or pass in an intersection. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers trying to enter the same lane.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway, enter or exit a highway, or make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After turning, which lane should your car be in?

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete your turn in the left lane, which is closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beams when driving in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you might follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will bounce back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off the ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully, without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the engine carefully by moving the ignition switch just enough to stop the engine, not lock the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: A vehicle with high beams is coming toward you. Where should you look?

options.text: The right side of the road.
The left side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road when an oncoming vehicle has high beams on. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you stay on your course.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have ABS brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Hold down the brake pedal hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump your brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. It helps you stop fast and still steer your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots when changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to look over your shoulder before every lane change. This is the best way to check your blind spots.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location. It is illegal and unsafe to turn right where this sign is posted.
